title: Complaints Leading to Ban on Formaldehyde in Paints for Interior of Buildings and Proposal for Similar Ban on Paints for Furniture
what_it_is: Complaints Leading to Ban on Formaldehyde in Paints for Interior of Buildings and Proposal for Similar Ban on Paints for Furniture

sections.label: Formaldehyde in interior paints regulation
sections.summary: From 1 January 2026, interior paints with formaldehyde cannot be sold in Singapore, with penalties for offenders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: Since 2020, the National Environment Agency (NEA) has received 19 feedback cases on formaldehyde levels arising from renovation works.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: From 1 January 2026, interior paints with formaldehyde will not be allowed for sale in Singapore. "Formaldehyde in Paint" will be regulated as a hazardous substance under the Environmental Protection and Management Act (EPMA).

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: Companies found importing, manufacturing, possessing for the purpose of selling or offering for sale in Singapore, interior paints with formaldehyde levels equal to or exceeding 0.01% weight in weight, are, upon conviction, liable to a fine of up to $50,000 or imprisonment for a term up to two years or both.

sections.label: NEA studying formaldehyde issue
sections.summary: NEA is studying the issue, including reviewing international best practices, guidelines and regulatory requirements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: NEA is actively studying this issue, including the review of international best practices, guidelines and regulatory requirements.

sections.label: Ventilation advice and furniture review
sections.summary: Occupants are advised to improve ventilation, and NEA is reviewing formaldehyde treatments on wooden furniture.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: If products containing formaldehyde are installed in indoor spaces, occupants are advised to improve ventilation and promote air circulation by opening doors and windows where possible, as well as utilising fans and ventilation systems, which can help dilute the concentration of formaldehyde in those areas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: He mentioned that NEA is conducting a review of formaldehyde treatments on wooden furniture.

sections.label: Balancing public health and industry
sections.summary: The approach balances protecting public health with how the industry can adapt to new requirements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: Like what we did for the formaldehyde controls in paints, we strike a balance between protecting public health as well as how the industry is able to adapt to the new requirements, because any changes may affect the industry and ultimately, consumers if they are not able to respond accordingly.

sections.label: Feedback cases smell nuisance
sections.summary: Of the 19 feedback cases, a lot mainly dealt with cases of smell nuisance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: Based on the 19 feedback cases I mentioned earlier, a lot mainly dealt with cases of smell nuisance.

sections.label: Question on regulating furniture
sections.summary: A question asks whether furniture can be included in the regulations since that regulation has not come on board.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Since that regulation has not come on board, can we include furniture as well in the regulations?
